result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick sensible numbers (68ch reading measure, a capped frame, a wider column for code and tables) and both make code and tables scroll inside their own boxes. In both, a `.wide` block placed inside `.prose` stays at 68ch instead of breaking out as claimed; A at least says to put wide blocks outside `.prose`. B has more problems: `.grid-tiers` never sets `display: grid` unless it is also given `.grid`, the 12-column grid only uses spans 12, 6 and 4, the 1440px breakpoint only changes the gutter, and its 'never orphaned' claim fails for three items on tablet. A is leaner and handles 3- and 4-tier pricing on purpose. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B wins narrowly. It separates feature rows (text beside media) from card and pricing grids, uses clamp() gutters and gaps that need fewer breakpoint overrides, and gives a concrete wide-monitor check. Both answers wrongly suggest code can be wider than the prose column while still nested inside it. B's HTML comment says this outright, though its prose then says to put wide blocks outside .prose. A's 1440 breakpoint only changes the gutter, and its 12-column grid is more machinery than these pages need.
